claim.qualifier: GM markets 'up to 381 mi' for the Hummer EV Pickup with the 24-module battery pack (~205 kWh). This trim is classified as heavy-duty (>8,500 lb GVWR) and is exempt from EPA range certification.
claim.verbatim_quote: Pickup EV3X, 24‑module, 22" wheels — ~205 kWh — Up to 381 mi (GM est.) — Heavy‑duty classification; no EPA window sticker.

reality.qualifier: Real-world highway testing on the 24-module pack pickup with all-terrain tires shows 260–320 mi at 70 mph. Per Recharged synthesis: 'Long-range king; Off-Road package and MT tires trim range.' One independent 75 mph loop test of a Pickup Edition 1 (24-module) measured ~290 mi.
reality.verbatim_quote: Pickup Edition 1 — 24-module pack — GM-est. 329–355 mi (depending on year/options) — ~290 mi @ 75 mph — Independently tested at about 290 miles on a 75‑mph loop before stopping

sources.name: Recharged — GMC Hummer EV Real-World Highway Range

narrative_one_liner: GM markets 381 mi for the 24-module Hummer EV pickup; this trim has no EPA window sticker — exempt due to heavy-duty classification.
narrative: GMC advertises 'up to 381 miles' for the long-range Hummer EV Pickup 3X (24-module battery pack). This vehicle is classified as heavy-duty (>8,500 lb GVWR) and is therefore exempt from EPA range certification. The 381-mi figure is GM's own estimate, not independently validated by the EPA test cycle. Real-world independent testing shows 260–320 mi at typical highway speeds. Buyers comparing this number against EPA-certified competitors (e.g., Rivian R1T 410 mi EPA, Silverado EV 450 mi EPA) are comparing apples to oranges — a manufacturer estimate against EPA-validated numbers.
methodology_notes: Categorical gap because the issue is not a pure measurement discrepancy but a regulatory framework difference. The 381 mi may itself be optimistic, but more importantly it lacks the EPA test-cycle validation that 'window sticker' implies.
caveats: The 318 mi EPA figure for the 2X trim (170 kWh) is EPA-certified. The deception is about the 3X trim (24-module, 205 kWh), which is the one GM advertises with the 381 mi number.
Heavy-duty exemption applies to all manufacturers; this is not Hummer-specific. Other heavy-duty exempt EVs (Cybertruck — partially) face the same issue.
Severity 'high' rests on the buyer-comparison-distortion harm; safety implications are minimal.
alternative_explanations: GM may have applied EPA-equivalent methodology internally; without published test methodology this cannot be verified.
Heavy-duty classification is a regulatory choice driven by GVWR/utility, not deception — but the marketing presentation conflates the two regimes.
